title: Jira Workload
description: Tile: Jira Workload. Same data points as Jira's own native Workload report -- Agent, Work Items In Progress -- for one Jira project, scoped via an explicit `project_key` the same way Jira's own Workload report itself is a per-project report, not a site-wide one. The originating ticket said 'Action: No Actions', but a follow-up request added row click-through: clicking an agent opens Jira's own issue navigator (`https://<site>/issues/?jql=...`) pre-filtered to that agent's own in-progress work in this project (`assignee = "<accountId>" AND project = <project_key> AND statusCategory = "In Progress"`). The full URL is pre-built per row inside `atlassian_workload_by_agent` itself (as a `searchUrl` field), not computed at click time -- a `Table`'s `rowAction.fromRow` can only pull an already-resolved field off the row, it can't invoke a `$computed` itself. `site_url`/`project_key` are both plain literal args passed into that function (hardcoded to the sandbox, `https://mysmb.atlassian.net` / `KAN`) -- same per-tenant-manual-edit limitation already accepted for `service_desk_id`/`project_key` everywhere else in this connector; there's no cheap way to resolve a browsable site URL from within a single dataProvider call. Built entirely on the existing `search_issues` tool (JQL `project = <project_key> AND statusCategory = "In Progress"`, `fields: ["assignee"]`, `max_results: 100`) -- no new server-side tool needed. `atlassian_workload_by_agent` (this plugin's widget-elements) groups the returned issues by `fields.assignee.accountId`, counting one work item per issue, and returns them sorted most-work-items-first. Two exclusions, both per the ticket's explicit ask for 'only human user accounts': issues with a `null` assignee (unassigned -- doesn't belong to anyone's workload) are dropped entirely, and any assignee whose `accountType` isn't `"atlassian"` (Atlassian's own Jira Cloud Platform REST API v3 User resource docs: `"atlassian"` = real human user, `"app"` = Connect/Forge/automation account, `"customer"` = JSM-only customer account) is excluded as a non-human 'inbuilt agent'. **Honesty note, not a hedge to gloss over:** the exclusion path itself (`accountType !== "atlassian"`) is UNTESTED against a live example -- this sandbox has an 'Automatic' account that appears in Jira's assignee-picker UI but could not actually be assigned to a real issue through that UI (selecting it silently reverted to Unassigned), so there was no way to produce a real non-"atlassian"-accountType assignee to confirm this filter against. Only the human-agent path (accountType `"atlassian"`) was confirmed live. See `atlassian_workload_by_agent`'s own JSDoc in `widget-elements/src/index.ts` for the full reasoning, including a 2019 Atlassian Developer Community report of `accountType` sometimes misreporting app accounts as `"atlassian"` (unconfirmed whether still current). Capped at 20 rows per `TILE-DISPLAY-STANDARDS.md` §11 (irrelevant in practice for a single project's human-agent roster, kept for consistency). `search_issues` defaults to 50 results, capped at 100 max, paginated via `nextPageToken` -- a widget's `dataProvider` fires exactly one call, so this tile requests the max (`max_results: 100`) and checks the response's `isLast` flag: when `false`, more In-Progress issues exist beyond the 100 fetched, and the tile discloses that plainly (per §13's data-governance veracity principle, the same honesty pattern as the SLA%-this-month action's own truncation disclosure) rather than presenting a partial per-agent count as complete.
